# Command line

<!-- Generated by scripts/gen-cli-docs.sh from `devsync --help`. Do not edit by hand. -->

Every command accepts the global options `-C <dir>` (run as if started in
`<dir>`), `--json` (machine-readable output), `-v` (verbose) and `-q`
(quiet). Commands find the project by looking for `.devsync.toml` in the
current directory and its parents.

| Command | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| [`init`](#devsync-init) | Create .devsync.toml in the current directory |
| [`push`](#devsync-push) | Make the remote tree match the local one |
| [`watch`](#devsync-watch) | Push on every save; collect results of running jobs. Keeps working offline |
| [`exec`](#devsync-exec) | Sync, run a command remotely, show its output, pull back changed files [alias: run] |
| [`submit`](#devsync-submit) | Sync and start a command remotely without waiting; prints the job id [alias: bg] |
| [`logs`](#devsync-logs) | Show a job's output (default: the latest job), following it while it runs |
| [`jobs`](#devsync-jobs) | List jobs |
| [`kill`](#devsync-kill) | Stop a running job (default: the latest) |
| [`collect`](#devsync-collect) | Fetch output of running jobs into .devsync/jobs/ once, then exit |
| [`pull`](#devsync-pull) | Get code from the remote: the whole project (safe) or a given path |
| [`status`](#devsync-status) | Configuration, connectivity and pending changes |
| [`changes`](#devsync-changes) | Local changes not yet on the remote, like `git status` (no network) |
| [`doctor`](#devsync-doctor) | Check the whole setup end to end and explain problems |
| [`forward`](#devsync-forward) | Forward remote ports to localhost (reconnects automatically) |
| [`shell`](#devsync-shell) | Interactive shell in the matching remote directory |
| [`setup`](#devsync-setup) | Install coding-agent integration |
| [`completions`](#devsync-completions) | Print shell completions |

## devsync

```text
Edit locally, run remotely. Sync and remote execution built for flaky connections.

Usage: devsync [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  init         Create .devsync.toml in the current directory
  push         Make the remote tree match the local one
  watch        Push on every save; collect results of running jobs. Keeps working offline
  exec         Sync, run a command remotely, show its output, pull back changed files [alias: run]
  submit       Sync and start a command remotely without waiting; prints the job id [alias: bg]
  logs         Show a job's output (default: the latest job), following it while it runs
  jobs         List jobs
  kill         Stop a running job (default: the latest)
  collect      Fetch output of running jobs into .devsync/jobs/ once, then exit
  pull         Get code from the remote: the whole project (safe) or a given path
  status       Configuration, connectivity and pending changes
  changes      Local changes not yet on the remote, like `git status` (no network)
  doctor       Check the whole setup end to end and explain problems
  forward      Forward remote ports to localhost (reconnects automatically)
  shell        Interactive shell in the matching remote directory
  setup        Install coding-agent integration
  completions  Print shell completions
  help         Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
  -C, --dir <DIR>  Run as if started in this directory
      --json       Machine-readable output (NDJSON events / JSON results)
  -v, --verbose    Show every file transferred and connection details
  -q, --quiet      Only errors and warnings
  -h, --help       Print help
  -V, --version    Print version

Start with: devsync init user@host:~/project   then: devsync exec -- <command>
```

## devsync init

```text
Create .devsync.toml in the current directory

Usage: devsync init [OPTIONS] <TARGET>

Arguments:
  <TARGET>  user@host:/remote/path (or local:/path for a local agent)

Options:
  -C, --dir <DIR>  Run as if started in this directory
      --force      Overwrite an existing config
      --json       Machine-readable output (NDJSON events / JSON results)
  -v, --verbose    Show every file transferred and connection details
  -q, --quiet      Only errors and warnings
  -h, --help       Print help
```

## devsync push

```text
Make the remote tree match the local one

Usage: devsync push [OPTIONS]

Options:
  -C, --dir <DIR>  Run as if started in this directory
  -n, --dry-run    Show what would change without transferring
      --force      Allow deleting more than sync.max_delete remote files
      --json       Machine-readable output (NDJSON events / JSON results)
  -v, --verbose    Show every file transferred and connection details
  -q, --quiet      Only errors and warnings
  -h, --help       Print help
```

## devsync exec

```text
Sync, run a command remotely, show its output, pull back changed files

Usage: devsync exec [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>...

Arguments:
  <COMMAND>...  Command (use `--` before it if it has flags)

Options:
  -C, --dir <DIR>     Run as if started in this directory
      --no-push       Skip the sync before running
      --json          Machine-readable output (NDJSON events / JSON results)
      --no-pull-back  Do not bring back files the command changed
  -v, --verbose       Show every file transferred and connection details
  -q, --quiet         Only errors and warnings
  -h, --help          Print help
```

## devsync pull

```text
Get code from the remote: the whole project (safe) or a given path.

Without a path: bring the remote's changes into this project. Files only on the remote, or that you haven't edited since the last sync, are updated; files you edited keep your version and the remote one is saved as <file>.devsync-remote. Sync excludes apply.

With a path: copy that remote file or directory exactly (overwriting local copies; excludes don't apply).

Usage: devsync pull [OPTIONS] [PATH] [DEST]

Arguments:
  [PATH]
          Path relative to the remote project root (omit to pull the whole project safely)

  [DEST]
          Local directory to place it under (default: project root; only with a path)

Options:
  -C, --dir <DIR>
          Run as if started in this directory

  -n, --dry-run
          Show what would change without downloading

      --json
          Machine-readable output (NDJSON events / JSON results)

  -v, --verbose
          Show every file transferred and connection details

  -q, --quiet
          Only errors and warnings

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
```

## devsync setup

```text
Install coding-agent integration

Usage: devsync setup [OPTIONS] <WHAT>

Arguments:
  <WHAT>
          Possible values:
          - claude:    Claude Code hook + CLAUDE.md instructions
          - agents-md: AGENTS.md instructions (Codex, Cursor, others)
          - all:       Everything above

Options:
  -C, --dir <DIR>
          Run as if started in this directory

      --json
          Machine-readable output (NDJSON events / JSON results)

  -v, --verbose
          Show every file transferred and connection details

  -q, --quiet
          Only errors and warnings

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
```
